summary: New hires intermittently receive 403 on internal console for 1-3 minutes after onboarding due to SSO handshake delay and delayed RBAC assertion
description:
Issue summary:
- Several recent new-employee support tickets report an immediate 403 when trying to access the internal Support Console and internal dashboards for a short window (typically 60–180s) after account provisioning.

Impact:
- Affects newly provisioned users (onboarding flow) across org units; blocks first-login flows and automated onboarding checks.
- Intermittent but reproducible: if user waits ~2–3 minutes or reauths, access is granted.

Environment:
- Production (us-west) identity-proxy + Okta as IdP. RBAC evaluation service and support-console behind identity-proxy.

Observed behaviour / steps to reproduce:
1) Provision new employee via Okta JIT provisioning / SCIM with role assignment.
2) New user signs in using SSO, Okta issues assertion and redirects to identity-proxy.
3) Support Console returns 403 on initial login attempt for ~60–180s.
4) Re-trying the login or waiting results in successful access and expected RBAC roles.

Initial logs attached (excerpt):
- identity-proxy logs (auth handshakes): "200 OK, assertion cached=false, role-lookup=miss, forwarded-role-header=absent" timestamped at user login time.
- rbac-service logs: "no roles found for principal xyz (fresh-scim-id), cache-miss" followed immediately by a later entry: "roles resolved: [support:viewer]" after ~90s.
- Okta audit shows assertion issued at T0 and SCIM provisioning complete around T0-5s to T0+10s.

Hypothesis:
- Race between SCIM provisioning (or user creation in internal identity store) and the first SSO assertion that triggers RBAC resolution. The identity-proxy allows the assertion through but the RBAC service returns empty because user indexes are not yet consistent/visible. A short window exists where login succeeds to IdP level but RBAC claims are not yet present, producing 403.

Business context / urgency:
- This impacts new-hire onboarding and support engineers who verify new accounts. It is high-touch and time-sensitive for People Ops. Raising to P1 to avoid repeated manual escalations and shadowing across teams.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a SCIM/Okta user with role mapping (simulate new hire)
Immediately attempt SSO login to support-console from a fresh browser session
Observe 403 response and capture identity-proxy + rbac-service logs for the principal
Wait 2-3 minutes or force a reauth and confirm access is granted
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10: Triage by SRE and Identity. Verified logs for three independent new-hire repros from 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10. Pattern: SCIM create success followed by immediate SSO assertion where rbac-service returned empty roles.

2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging by introducing artificial timing: delayed SCIM finalization vs immediate SSO assertion. Confirmed that TTL on rbac-service index write was ~30s in the worst case (replication to read index).

Telemetry: ~14% of new user sign-ins within the first 2 minutes after provisioning see the 403; rate increases when provisioning spikes (e.g., bulk new hires).

Edge cases identified: role-mapping evaluation relies on a secondary user-index service that lags under load by 30-120s. identity-proxy does not currently retry RBAC lookup on cache-miss before returning 403.

Temporary mitigations tried: 1) Forcing identity-proxy to defer final login by 15s produces consistent success but adds noticeable latency and is not acceptable as a long-term UX fix. 2) People Ops advised to pause automated verification jobs for 2 minutes post-provisioning (manual workaround).
comments: Elena Martinez (reporter) 2026-03-10: Filed after 4 onboarding tickets this morning. Attaching sample logs and onboarding timestamps.
Ravi Kapoor (assignee) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Will reproduce in staging and trace SCIM -> index -> rbac flow. Adding identity-proxy and rbac-service owners.

SRE-Lead (Harper Chen) 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging with timing harness. User-index write lag observed under concurrent provisioning load. Suggest investigating eventual consistency window in indexer service.
Identity-Eng (Maya Patel) 2026-03-11: Found that indexer bulk-write batched commits every 15s; under load batches got spaced into 45–90s due to GC pauses on the indexer node.
resolution_notes:
Status: In Progress. Proposed multi-pronged remediation: 1) Short-term: update identity-proxy to treat RBAC "no roles found" on a fresh principal as a transient state and perform up to 2 retry attempts with exponential backoff (500ms -> 1000ms) before returning 403. 2) Medium-term: change indexer commit strategy to flush immediately for new user creation events originating from SCIM (config flag already exists but not enabled for SCIM path). 3) Long-term: add synchronous confirmation path for JIT/SCIM provisioning that marks the user ready to handle immediate assertions, or queue assertions for up to 5s.

Implementation notes: identity-proxy PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/879 (adds retry and improved logging). Indexer change tracked in internal ticket INT-202704.

Follow-ups: run a 48-hour canary with retry-enabled identity-proxy and monitor new-hire first-login success metric. Update People Ops runbook to include 30s passive wait as a stopgap. Will update ticket when canary completes and if metrics show <1% failure window.
notes_for_oncall: If alerted about new-hire 403s, check identity-proxy logs for 'role-lookup=miss' and whether retry attempts occurred. If indexer shows backlog, escalate to Indexer-oncall. Avoid immediate user reprovisioning as it can exacerbate batched indexer delays.
